name: Residential Dryer Vent Cleaning

symptoms: Clothes take 2 to 3 full cycles to dry completely
Top and sides of clothes dryer feel excessively hot to the touch

Visual camera borescopic inspection of duct interior and connection points

Post-cleaning CFM airflow verification and thermal safety check

faqs.question: How often should a residential dryer vent be professionally cleaned?
faqs.answer: The US Fire Administration (USFA) and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) recommend having your dryer vent inspected and cleaned at least once every 12 months. Homes with large families running 5+ loads weekly, pets shedding hair, or vent duct runs exceeding 25 feet should clean them every 6 to 9 months.

faqs.question: Does cleaning the lint trap prevent dryer fires?
faqs.answer: No. While clearing the lint screen before every load is essential, lint screens capture only 40% to 60% of airborne fibers. The rest passes through the blower wheel into the exhaust ductwork, where it accumulates on pipe walls and creates an explosive tinderbox.

faqs.question: Can clean dryer vents really lower my electric bill?
faqs.answer: Yes. When a vent is clogged, your dryer operates for 90 to 120 minutes instead of 40 minutes per load. Professional lint clearing restores unrestricted airflow, saving average households $18 to $24 per month ($216 - $288 annually) in electricity or gas consumption.

faqs.question: Why do rooftop dryer vents clog much faster than side-wall vents?
faqs.answer: Rooftop vents force hot, moist lint air to travel vertically against gravity (often 15 to 30 feet). As the air rises and cools, moisture condenses on metal duct walls, turning loose lint into sticky, cement-like sludge that coats the pipe and rapidly closes the airway.

faqs.question: Do your technicians have OSHA-compliant safety equipment for steep roofs?
faqs.answer: Yes. All our certified technicians carry OSHA-approved ladder stabilizers, roof pitch anchors, and safety harnesses to service single-story, two-story, and steep-slope residential roofs safely.

name: Dryer Vent Repair & Replacement
hero_description: Code-compliant replacement of ripped, crushed foil or hazardous plastic transition hoses with rigid, fire-rated UL 2158A smooth metal ductwork.
symptoms: White vinyl, flexible plastic, or corrugated foil accordion hose behind dryer
Visible duct punctures, crushed sections, or detached joints in crawlspace/attic
Dryer pushed back against the wall, kinking or flattening the transition hose
Carbon monoxide detector sounding near gas dryer installations
Lint accumulation behind drywall, baseboards, or under laundry room subfloors
diagnostic_steps: Comprehensive IRC Section M1502 residential building code compliance audit
Smoke pen leak detection test at all duct seams, elbows, and drywall penetrations
Removal and safe disposal of non-code vinyl or crushed accordion flex ducts
Installation of 26-gauge rigid smooth-wall galvanized steel or aluminum piping
Metallic foil tape sealing (zero screws penetrating duct interior to prevent lint snags)

faqs.question: Why are plastic or thin foil dryer hoses illegal in modern building codes?
faqs.answer: Under International Residential Code (IRC M1502), flexible plastic and unlisted vinyl ducts are strict fire code violations because they melt easily and act as an accelerant during a lint fire. Rigid smooth-walled metal pipe contains fires and prevents lint accumulation.

faqs.question: Can screws be used to connect dryer duct sections?
faqs.answer: Never. Screws that penetrate the inside of a dryer duct act as lint catchers, rapidly snagging fibers and causing severe blockages. International building codes require seams to be mechanically connected with non-penetrating clamps and sealed with UL-listed aluminum foil tape.

name: Dryer Vent Rerouting & Optimization
hero_description: Redesigning overly long, excessively bent, or poorly routed dryer ductwork to achieve the shortest, straightest, and safest path to outdoor exhaust.
symptoms: Duct run exceeds 35 equivalent feet with multiple 90-degree elbows
Duct exhausts into an attic, crawlspace, garage, or chimney rather than outdoors
Dryer runs hot because excessive backpressure chokes the blower motor
Frequent recurring clogs requiring service every 2-3 months
Remodeling or relocating washer and dryer to an interior room
diagnostic_steps: Total equivalent length engineering calculation (accounting for elbows and dampers)
Core drilling new exterior penetration through brick, stucco, siding, or foundation
Rerouting ductwork along joists to eliminate unnecessary 90-degree sharp bends
Installation of smooth-sweep 45-degree elbows to maximize continuous airflow
Exterior weather-sealed damper hood installation with animal protection

faqs.question: What is the maximum allowed length for a dryer exhaust duct?
faqs.answer: Under standard building codes (IRC M1502.4.6.1), the maximum developed duct run is 35 feet from dryer connection to outdoor exhaust. Each 90-degree elbow reduces this maximum by 5 feet, and each 45-degree elbow reduces it by 2.5 feet. If your run exceeds this, rerouting or a booster fan is mandatory.

Exterior dryer vent flap broken, stuck open, or missing entirely

diagnostic_steps: Inspection of exterior termination hood and assessment of nest depth
Safe extraction of nesting materials, bird droppings, and debris using retrieval hooks

faqs.question: Why do birds and rodents choose dryer vents for nesting?
faqs.answer: Dryer exhaust ducts provide warm, elevated, sheltered cavities that protect birds (especially European starlings and sparrows) and squirrels from predators and cold weather. In spring, uncapped vents are prime nesting targets.

faqs.question: Can I put standard window wire mesh over my dryer vent?
faqs.answer: No! Standard fine wire mesh will quickly catch airborne lint, creating a 100% clog and immediate fire hazard within weeks. Code requires specially designed dryer pest guards with weighted louver flaps or wide-gap bar grates that let lint escape while barring animals.

name: Dryer Exhaust Booster Fan Installation

symptoms: Duct run exceeds 35 feet and cannot be rerouted due to home architectural layout

diagnostic_steps: Static pressure sensor audit along the entire duct length

faqs.question: How does a dryer booster fan know when to turn on?
faqs.answer: Modern DEDPV booster fans feature an integrated electronic pressure sensor or current-sensing relay. When the clothes dryer turns on and begins blowing air, the sensor automatically detects positive pressure and activates the booster fan, maintaining a minimum 1,200 FPM air velocity.
